limits: JFR ExecutionSample and async-profiler CPU stacks are sampled stack shares, not wall time or total process CPU.
Inclusive frame percentages overlap. First matching scope wins only in disjoint scope tables.
ObjectAllocationSample weights estimate allocation churn; they are not retained heap or exact allocated bytes.
Process CPU is kernel utime+stime for the analyzer JVM, including native GC/JIT work. Boundary values interpolate roughly 1 s samples; the manifest UTC anchor has 1 s resolution.
STW pauses are wall-time intervals, not GC CPU. Do not subtract them from process CPU or turn sample shares into seconds.
JFR collection sumOfPauses is assigned by collection start; top-level GCPhasePause/gc.log intervals are intersected with windows separately.
A collapsed profile has no event timestamps. A mixed capture cannot be divided into per-run sample shares.
Run marker windows use logged clocks; engine/static-completion splitting also uses logged bindingTime. Partial/end snapshots can omit earlier events.
Cumulative counters, batch/packet events, admitted rows, CPU samples, allocation weights, RSS and retained heap have different units. Callback counts can vary with batching.
Different recordings can contain duplicate events. Never sum cumulative snapshots or overlapping windows.
